patient.name: Emily Cortez
patient.chiefComplaint: Active labor, 37 weeks, footling breech presentation, already crowning

history.hpi: 24-year-old G2P1 at 37 weeks gestation called 911 after a sudden urge to push at home. Contractions have been roughly 2 minutes apart for the last 20 minutes. On exam, a single fetal foot is visible at the vaginal opening rather than the head.
pastMedical: Uncomplicated prior vaginal delivery 3 years ago
history.events: Patient felt a sudden urge to push at home; husband called 911 when he saw a foot presenting at the vaginal opening

scene.dispatch: 24-year-old female, active labor, patient states baby is coming, residence
scene.location: Second-floor apartment bedroom, patient on bed
visualCues: Single fetal foot visible at the vaginal introitus
Strong contractions visibly gripping the patient every 2 minutes
Prenatal records folder on the nightstand showing 37-week gestation

phases.name: Initial Contact
phases.description: Crew arrives to find a 24-year-old female in active labor with a single fetal foot presenting at the vaginal opening — a footling breech — with strong contractions every 2 minutes.

clinicalPresentation.airway: Patent, speaking full sentences between contractions
clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Intact, patient positioning herself for delivery
otherFindings: Single fetal foot presenting at vaginal introitus
No prolapsed cord visible at this time
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "It's coming, I can feel it, please help me — something feels different this time!"

expectedActions.shortAction: Position mother supine; allow buttocks, feet, and trunk to deliver spontaneously without traction
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Breech Birth: Place mother supine, allow the buttocks, feet, and trunk to deliver spontaneously, then support the body while the head is delivered
expectedActions.rationale: Pulling on a breech fetus risks nuchal arm entrapment, cervical spine injury, or head entrapment.

expectedActions.shortAction: Assess for prolapsed cord as the trunk delivers; treat immediately if present
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Assess for presence of prolapsed cord and treat as above
expectedActions.rationale: Footling breech carries a higher risk of cord prolapse than cephalic or complete breech presentations.

expectedActions.shortAction: Support fetal body without pulling; keep fetus elevated off the umbilical cord
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Once the legs are delivered support the body to avoid hyperextension of the head; keep the fetus elevated off the umbilical cord
expectedActions.rationale: Prevents head hyperextension and cord compression during the vulnerable trunk-to-head interval.

transitions.condition: Crew recognizes footling breech presentation and positions the mother supine, allowing the buttocks, feet, and trunk to deliver spontaneously without applying traction.
Instead of allowing spontaneous descent, the crew pulls on the fetal trunk to hasten delivery, risking nuchal arm entrapment or cervical injury.

phases.name: Hands-off breech technique used
phases.description: The crew allows the buttocks, feet, and trunk to deliver spontaneously without pulling, continuously checking for a prolapsed cord and supporting the fetal body to prevent hyperextension of the head.
phases.triggerCondition: Crew recognizes the footling breech presentation and, per protocol, allows spontaneous delivery of the lower body without traction while assessing for cord complications.

otherFindings: Buttocks, feet, and trunk delivered spontaneously without traction
Umbilical cord palpated, pulsatile, no prolapse
Fetal body supported and kept elevated off the cord
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "Is the baby okay? Please don't pull!"

expectedActions.shortAction: Insert gloved hand, form a 'V' with index/ring fingers on infant's cheeks, flex chin to chest to create an airway and deliver the head
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: If head fails to deliver, place gloved hand into vagina with fingers between infant's face and uterine wall to create an open airway. Place your index and ring fingers on the baby's cheeks forming a "V" taking care not to block the mouth and allowing the chin to be tilted toward the chest flexing the neck
expectedActions.rationale: Creates an airway for the fetal face and flexes the head to allow safe passage through the birth canal.

transitions.condition: The head does not deliver spontaneously after the trunk, requiring the crew to create an airway and flex the fetal head per the protocol's breech head-delivery technique.

phases.name: Head delivered with jaw-flexion technique
phases.description: The fetal head fails to deliver spontaneously after the trunk. The crew creates an airway with a gloved hand and flexes the head using the jaw-flexion (Mauriceau-style) maneuver described in protocol.
phases.triggerCondition: After trunk delivery, the head does not deliver spontaneously, requiring the crew to place a gloved hand into the vagina to create an airway and flex the fetal head toward the chest.

otherFindings: Fetal head delivered using jaw-flexion technique
Newborn crying immediately after head delivery
Cord clamped and cut after 1 minute per protocol
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "I hear crying — is that my baby?"

expectedActions.shortAction: Dry, warm, and stimulate newborn; wrap in towel and place on maternal chest
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Dry, warm, and stimulate infant, wrap in towel and place on maternal chest unless resuscitation needed
expectedActions.rationale: Prevents neonatal hypothermia and promotes spontaneous respiratory effort.

expectedActions.shortAction: Record APGAR score at 1 and 5 minutes once neonate is stabilized
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Resuscitation takes priority over recording APGAR scores. Record APGAR scores at 1 and 5 minutes once neonate is stabilized
expectedActions.rationale: Documents neonatal transition status and guides any escalation to resuscitation.

expectedActions.shortAction: Notify medical direction/receiving facility of the breech presentation prior to arrival
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Notify medical direction/receiving facility if: ... Breech presentation
expectedActions.rationale: Allows the receiving facility to prepare an OB/neonatal team in advance.

transitions.condition: Newborn is delivered, dried, warmed, and stimulated; APGAR scoring and transport preparation begin.

phases.name: Newborn dried, warmed, APGAR scored
phases.description: The newborn is delivered, dried, warmed, and placed on the maternal chest. APGAR scores are recorded and the crew prepares mother and newborn for transport, notifying medical direction of the breech presentation.
phases.triggerCondition: After successful delivery of the head, the newborn is dried, warmed, and stimulated, then APGAR scored and prepared for transport with the mother.

otherFindings: Newborn crying vigorously, pink centrally, active movement
Cord clamped and cut, placenta not yet delivered

phases.name: Traction applied on fetal body
phases.description: The crew pulls on the fetal trunk attempting to hasten delivery instead of allowing spontaneous descent, creating risk of nuchal arm entrapment or cervical spine injury to the fetus.
phases.triggerCondition: Instead of a hands-off approach, the crew applies traction to the fetal body during descent, against the explicit protocol warning.

otherFindings: Delivery progress stalled after excessive traction applied to fetal trunk
Arm now entrapped behind the fetal neck, delaying head delivery
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "Something's wrong, it hurts so much more now!"

expectedActions.shortAction: Recognize impaired progress; stop traction and revert to a hands-off, support-only technique
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: NEVER pull on the body, especially a preterm or previable baby – just support the baby's body while mother pushes when she feels the urge to
expectedActions.rationale: Traction is the direct cause of nuchal arm entrapment; stopping it and allowing maternal effort to resume progress is the correction.
